fields.title: Polka: the tail that doesn't belong to us
fields.summary: Checkout p99 is 11 seconds, of which 8.4 seconds belong to the provider. Peak drop-off is 19%.
fields.decisionPrompt: What do we do? State the cost of your decision.
fields.brief/role: You are the Polka product manager.
fields.brief/company: Polka is a fictional grocery delivery service from local stores: 900 partner stores, a buyer app, and a partner portal.
fields.brief/context: You are the Polka product manager. Order placement: p50 = 640 ms, p95 = 2.1 s, p99 = 11 s. The target of p95 ≤ 3 s is met. Drop-off on the payment screen is 19% during evening peak vs 6% during quiet hours.
fields.brief/objective: Remove waiting time that does not belong to us and clean up our own path.
fields.brief/constraints: Switching providers takes three months. Their SLA allows p95 up to 15 seconds.
fields.brief/task: Decide what to do and separate your part from someone else's.
fields.learnTakeaway/title: First figure out whose time you are optimizing
fields.learnTakeaway/body: The request tail almost always consists of someone else's time and your own, and they are fixed differently. Your own part is cheap to clean up: redundant calls, sequential requests instead of batching, leftovers from long-removed screens. Someone else's time cannot be sped up at all—you remove it from the waiting loop by turning a synchronous step into an asynchronous one, and pay for it with a change in product behavior.
fields.evidenceCards/0/content: Out of 11 seconds p99: payment provider 8.4 s, promo code check 180 ms (executed always, even without promo code), stock check 480 ms (12 sequential calls), recommendations call 140 ms (block removed from screen half a year ago), the rest is ours.
fields.evidenceCards/1/content: Provider. SLA: p95 up to 15 s. Replacement takes three months.
fields.evidenceCards/2/content: 20k checkouts per day. p99 — 200 people daily wait longer than 11 seconds.
fields.evidenceCards/3/content: Without the provider, p99 is about 2.6 s.
fields.decisionOptions/0/label: Remove extra calls and combine leftovers
fields.decisionOptions/0/description: Remove extra calls and combine leftovers. Three days. Removes 740 ms.
fields.decisionOptions/0/consequence: p95 improves noticeably, p99 barely changes — dominated by the provider. Peak drop-off will remain.
fields.decisionOptions/1/description: Three weeks. Order is created immediately, payment is confirmed via notification.
fields.decisionOptions/1/consequence: removes the provider from the waiting time. Drop-off should drop sharply — according to the table, the main loss happens after 8 seconds. Changes product behavior: the user leaves the screen without knowing the payment result.
fields.decisionOptions/2/consequence: eliminates the source. Solves nothing this quarter. The new provider may have its own tail.
fields.decisionOptions/3/label: Show honest waiting with escalation and ability to dismiss
fields.decisionOptions/3/description: Show honest waiting with escalation and ability to dismiss. One week.
fields.decisionOptions/3/consequence: does not speed up, improves perception and reduces abandonment. According to `IN1` data, already partially implemented. Does not eliminate 41% drop-off when waiting longer than 8 seconds.
fields.rubric/remediation/0/gap: Does not convert percentile into a headcount of people
fields.rubric/remediation/1/gap: Does not inspect tracing for redundant items
fields.rubric/remediation/2/gap: Sets goals without considering the tail
fields.rubric/remediation/3/gap: Request path is not broken down, so someone else's time is taken for your own
